title: Nvidia opens up Israeli-founded Run:ai software two years after $800 million acquisition
source_used: CTech (fetched by me, the main fetch returned 0 characters); cross-checked against NVIDIA Technical Blog "NVIDIA Run:ai Is Now Open Source as Part of NVIDIA DSX AI Factory Platform"
key_facts: Nvidia is making the full software platform of Israeli-founded Run:ai available as open source (CTech and Nvidia developer blog, 13 Oct 2026).
Nvidia acquired Run:ai in late 2024 for an estimated $800 million, after an eight-month regulatory review in the United States and Europe.
Run:ai software allocates computing capacity across AI workloads and can share GPU resources among workloads that do not need a whole chip.
The release includes the complete platform and four parts that can be adopted separately: KAI Scheduler, GPU Fractioning Operator, KAI Resource Management and Workload Map.
When Nvidia bought the company, founders Omri Geller and Dr. Ronen Dar said they planned to open-source the software.
The community product needs no paid Run:ai subscription or Nvidia support entitlement, but enterprise support is not included; Nvidia will keep selling commercial versions.
Nvidia's developer blog says eight partners, including Crusoe, Mirantis, Nebius and vCluster, are integrating the open source platform into their offerings.
quote_evidence: The move opens up technology Nvidia acquired in late 2024 for an estimated $800 million, following an eight-month regulatory review in the United States and Europe.
The release does not mean that every use of Run:ai is now free of charge or includes enterprise support.
Nvidia will continue to offer commercial versions through its enterprise AI products and supported cloud offerings.
why_it_matters_hint: Developers and cloud providers get the code of a tool meant to get more work out of costly AI chips.
notes: Confirmed by Nvidia's own developer blog and CTech. The $800 million is CTech's estimate.
